jobs.description: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: The Shock and Vibration Engineering team is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to support product qualification, reliability testing, and design validation activities across our portfolio of mechanical systems. This role provides an opportunity to work closely with design, manufacturing, and quality teams to ensure products meet performance, reliability, and customer requirements before release and shipment. The successful candidate will develop and execute test plans, perform shock and vibration testing, analyze results, and provide engineering recommendations to improve product designs. This position requires a strong combination of mechanical engineering knowledge, hands-on laboratory experience, and problem-solving skills. Engineers in this role are expected to actively participate in product development efforts, collaborating with cross-functional teams to identify root causes, drive corrective actions, and support continuous improvement initiatives. This is a highly hands-on position involving the setup and operation of test equipment, fixtures, instrumentation, and large-scale laboratory systems. The role requires the ability to safely lift and move materials weighing up to 40 pounds, operate overhead cranes and material handling equipment, and work with power tools and mechanical assemblies. Familiarity with Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) controls, laboratory safety practices, and data acquisition systems is beneficial. The ideal candidate is a self-motivated engineer who enjoys working both in the lab and with development teams, thrives in a collaborative environment, and is passionate about validating products and improving designs through testing and engineering analysis. We are seeking a hands-on Mechanical Engineer to join our Shock and Vibration Engineering team. In this role, you will be responsible for the testing, validation, and continuous improvement of mechanical designs to ensure product reliability, quality, and customer satisfaction. You will work closely with cross-functional engineering teams to evaluate product performance, identify design improvements, and validate products prior to shipment to customers. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate combines strong mechanical engineering fundamentals with practical laboratory and test experience. This position involves planning and executing shock, vibration, and environmental tests; analyzing test results; documenting findings; and providing recommendations to improve product design and manufacturability. The role requires hands-on interaction with laboratory equipment, test fixtures, and prototype hardware. This position includes operating specialized test equipment and large-scale systems, including overhead cranes and material handling equipment, in accordance with established safety procedures. Candidates should be comfortable working in a laboratory environment and capable of lifting and moving components weighing up to 40 pounds. Experience with power tools, instrumentation, data acquisition systems, and Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) controls is highly desirable. The successful candidate will thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced engineering environment and possess a passion for solving complex mechanical challenges through testing, analysis, and continuous improvement. QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Basic understanding of mechanical design principles, material properties, and manufacturing processes. Familiarity with engineering test methods, data collection, and analysis techniques. Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and test procedures. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to document and present technical findings. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, PowerPoint). PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with mechanical testing, reliability testing, or laboratory environments through internships, co-ops, academic projects, or prior employment. Familiarity with shock, vibration, environmental, or product qualification testing. Experience using CAD software such as SolidWorks, Creo, or similar tools. Knowledge of data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, and test equipment. Understanding of statistical analysis and basic engineering data interpretation. Experience using power tools, hand tools, and mechanical assembly techniques. Familiarity with Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) requirements and laboratory safety practices. Experience operating cranes, hoists, forklifts, or other material handling equipment is a plus. Demonstrated ability to work in a hands-on engineering environment and safely lift and move equipment weighing up to 40 pounds. KEY COMPETENCIES: Mechanical aptitude and hands-on troubleshooting skills. Attention to detail and commitment to safety and quality. Curiosity and desire to learn new technologies and test methodologies. Strong organizational and time management skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced engineering environment. About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality. Customers order their convenience, grocery, retail, and prepared foods in the DoorDash app, and our team members fulfill orders in a real, brick-and-mortar store for Dashers to deliver. We’re open early and close late - some sites even run 24/7!
About the Role
DashMart is looking for a motivated and experienced individual that excels in fast-paced, physical environments and is excited to roll up their sleeves and actively engage in day-to-day operations. In this role, you will work within a local fulfillment center supporting Site Management running great shifts, and delegating tasks. As a Shift Lead, you will have shift responsibility for fulfilling orders in a warehouse environment and maintaining inventory, and in some locations, this involves preparing food in a light-prep kitchen.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Be an Owner: Take ownership of your assigned shifts, including warehouse and kitchen processes, safety/cleanliness, quality, and training. Maintain accountability for inventory, equipment, and other company assets to ensure they are properly handled, stored, and protected from loss or theft.

Lead: Guide Operations Associates through their shift by ensuring the team works safely and productively and serving as the point of escalation for daily operations.

You will be expected to engage in professional and respectful interactions with team members and customers, ensuring a positive and safe atmosphere in the warehouse while providing a high-quality experience for our customers.

We’re excited about you because…
You’re self-motivated, positive, and a team player. You work well with others, and you bring a great attitude to your work each and every day. You have high integrity and are excited to delight customers.

You’re able to be on your feet and move heavy products. You are excited and physically able (with or without accommodation) to lift up to 50 lbs., depending on the needs of the specific site, and can operate a pallet jack and hand truck.

You have a high school diploma or GED equivalent. A college diploma is even better but not required.
You are at least 18 years of age.

You have flexibility in your schedule. Depending upon the scheduling needs of the hiring site, you can be available for a number of different shifts a week.

jobs.description: THE ASSOCIATE ROLE The Associate is the operational lead on LAS engagements and a genuine thought partner in the advisory process. Associates transform leadership data into business-relevant insights: identifying patterns in people and teams, determining what those patterns mean for organizational outcomes, and communicating those implications in ways that help clients make better talent decisions. Associates own workstreams end-to-end. They drive the project plan, conduct and support interviews and assessments, synthesize qualitative and quantitative data, write the reports and client materials, and keep engagements moving. They partner closely with Consultants, who own the client relationship and the final deliverable, while taking real accountability for quality, pace, and the client experience along the way. This is a role with meaningful ownership. It is also a support role in an apprenticeship model: Associates build credibility, judgment, and client exposure over time, and responsibility grows as that credibility is earned. WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY DO The work varies by Solution and by team, but the following responsibilities are consistent across the role. Insight development and client deliverables Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data from interviews, assessments, diagnostics, and secondary research to identify themes, insights, and implications Write and own client deliverables, Advanced Leadership Profile (ALP) and Leadership Profile (LP) assessment reports, group and comparison reports, culture and team diagnostic outputs, board materials, workshop decks, and executive summaries Draft assessment components independently, including Individual Style Profile (ISP), 360, capabilities, strengths and development opportunities, and summary pages; over time, contribute Executive Intelligence (ExI) insights Connect leadership insight to business context, company performance, value creation, role requirements, and the risks and opportunities facing the client Assessment, interviews, and client interaction Conduct and support executive and stakeholder interviews; lead, co-lead, or participate in assessments depending on the Solution, the engagement, and the Consultant Conduct 360 reference interviews and synthesize input into balanced, evidence-based summaries Lead internal calibration calls and contribute an informed, data-backed point of view on scoring and conclusions Participate in client debriefs, workshops, and readouts; over time, debrief participants and lead segments of client sessions Administer proprietary leadership advisory tools and diagnostics (ISP, culture, team effectiveness, and related instruments) in partnership with the Consultant, and analyze the resulting data Represent the Firm with professionalism, maturity, and poise in written, verbal, virtual, and in-person settings, and handle confidential information with discretion Engagement and project management Own the project plan and timeline end-to-end; organize and facilitate team touchpoints, including kick-offs, check-ins, and project recaps Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for the client alongside the Consultant, and draft client and stakeholder communications Organize and distribute work across the engagement team, clarify roles, and hold the team accountable to deadlines Anticipate what the client, Consultant, and team will need next; identify risks early, escalate appropriately, and propose a path forward Synthesize client meetings, board interactions, and workshops into clear themes, decisions, and next steps Manage several engagements at once across time zones and competing deadlines, and maintain your capacity tracker accurately so staffing decisions can be made well Use AI-enabled tools thoughtfully to improve efficiency in research, drafting, and summarization, always validating sources and conclusions, exercising judgment around client data and confidentiality, and retaining human accountability for the insight Developing others and building the practice Guide Analysts on first-draft documents, provide examples and standards, and give timely, constructive feedback Serve as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor to new colleagues and contribute to their integration Contribute to Solution and intellectual capital development, case studies, best practices, and internal tools Build relationships with Executive Search colleagues and help them understand where LAS can add value for their clients Occasionally support business development, contributing to qualifications decks, proposal materials, and background research. Associates are rarely involved in client pitches; that exposure typically comes at the Senior Associate level and beyond. YOUR FIRST YEAR We invest heavily in structured onboarding, and we expect training to take priority over client work in the early months. New Associates are not expected to take a project solo until they have demonstrated proficiency in that skill under the mentorship of an experienced colleague. A typical first-year path includes: Firm and LAS onboarding — understanding our business model, strategy, services, and how Search and LAS work together. Core curriculum — Insight Foundations, Insight Bootcamp, Overview of Capabilities, Culture in Action, the Leadership Model, the 360s course, Writing with Impact, and ExI Bootcamp. Assessment — shadow full ALPs; lead 360 interviews and write the page solo; write ISP and capabilities pages; write strengths, development opportunities, and summary pages; build toward delivering a full ALP report at roughly 80 percent client readiness. Organizational consulting — administer and analyze ISP, culture, and team effectiveness surveys; draft group and culture reports; debrief the culture graph; support workshop design, materials, and onsite coordination. Business acumen — how businesses make money, different operating and ownership models, organizational structures, C-suite roles and responsibilities, and basic financial literacy. This is supported by the LAS Business Acumen Series (Business Strategy, Financial Basics, Anatomy of a Company, Engagement and Client Management). Consulting skills — craft a credible introduction for clients, present informed opinions and defend them with data, professionally challenge the views of others, and proactively seek feedback from every project team. THE SUPPORT AROUND YOU You will not be left to figure this out alone. Every new Associate is supported by a defined team: Talent Partner — your manager, responsible for your development, staffing, and performance, with a recurring one-on-one cadence Onboarding mentor — a peer who helps you navigate the Firm, its systems, and its unwritten rules Apprenticeship mentors — one to two Associates or Senior Associates who are your first point of contact for client work; new hires are paired with a dedicated Consultant or Senior Associate capacity for the first six to twelve months, so you learn by apprenticeship Engagement teams — Consultants, Associates, and Executive Engagement Assistants who coach you in the flow of the work The AAPM community — the Associate & Analyst Practice Member group, which runs monthly calls, coffee chats, learning cafés, and peer development programming THE REALITIES OF THE ROLE We would rather be direct than have you discover these after you join. The workload is deadline-driven and uneven. Priorities are set by client needs and Consultant schedules. There are genuinely intense stretches around report deadlines, board readouts, and workshops, and quieter stretches in between. This is client service: timelines shift, clients reschedule, and there will be occasional work outside normal hours to meet a client commitment. Assessment work is rigorous. Spending several hours on camera with a participant and then multiple hours writing and nuancing a report is demanding. It is also core to what we do. We balance assessment with other work to give you a variety. Staffing is partially relationship-based. Opportunities are influenced by the connections, trust, and internal reputation you build. Early on, you will work on what the practice needs, which may not always be the work that energizes you most. Over time, you gain far more influence over the projects and people you work with, but you have to invest in the relationships to get there. The work is predominantly at the most senior levels. Because we work with C-suite executives and boards, there are fewer opportunities to independently lead assessments early on than at firms that work deeper in the organization. This also leads to what makes the role great (below). Autonomy can feel like ambiguity. You will be trusted to manage your own time and to choose work in partnership with your Talent Partner. Not every step will be laid out for you. The learning curve is real. Our methodology is complex, and our quality bar is high. Most Associates, including those with directly relevant prior experience, need several months before they feel confident with the tools, frameworks, and standards. That is expected. WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE WORTH IT Exposure to senior leaders and consequential decisions. Associates work directly on material that reaches C-suite executives, boards, and investors, and contributes to decisions that shape organizations. That exposure typically comes much later in a career elsewhere. Accelerated learning. You will see how successful leaders think, make decisions, and navigate complexity across many companies, industries, and situations in a fraction of the time it would take from inside a single organization. Exceptional colleagues. Our people are consistently named as the best part of working here: smart, generous with their time, deeply committed to quality, and invested in helping one another improve. Quality over volume. We prioritize thoughtful analysis, sound judgment, and exceptional work products over speed or scale. That creates a steeper learning curve and a far better development experience. Variety and breadth. Public and private companies across every major sector, and work spanning assessment, succession, culture, team effectiveness, development, and organizational effectiveness. Real ownership. You own workstreams, deliverables and client communications, and you have meaningful influence over your schedule, your projects and your career path. A developmental culture. Structured curriculum, apprenticeship mentoring, real-time feedback on every project, a published development framework and colleagues who are invested in your growth rather than competing with you. KEY RELATIONSHIPS Reports to Talent Partner (Leadership Advisory Services) Day-to-day direction Consultants and Senior Associates, on a per-engagement basis Career guidance Counselor (Consultant), onboarding mentor and apprenticeship mentors Other key relationships Analysts; Project Managers; Executive Engagement Assistants; Content Editors; Client Care Liaisons; Knowledge Management and Solution Support; Executive Search colleagues; the Associate & Analyst Practice Member (AAPM) community Location Based in one of our North American offices CANDIDATE PROFILE IDEAL EXPERIENCE Generally four or more years of relevant professional experience in leadership advisory, executive assessment, management or strategy consulting, organizational development, human capital or talent management, or a relevant industry role. Undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. An advanced degree (for example, in organizational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, business or a related field) is helpful but not required; relevant professional experience can substitute. Superior business writing skills, evidenced through project work or a writing sample provided on request Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information into clear, evidence-based insight Strong project management and organizational skills, with a track record of managing multiple priorities and competing deadlines General business acumen developed through exposure to a range of business situations and contexts Executive presence and interpersonal effectiveness; comfort interacting with senior leaders Client deliverables are written in English; superior English business writing is an essential function of the role. Additional languages are an advantage. Work authorization for the country in which you are applying WHO TENDS TO THRIVE HERE Intellectually curious people who want to understand the “why” behind people, businesses, and organizational outcomes, and who enjoy connecting disparate pieces of information into a point of view People who combine intellectual confidence with genuine humility, and who engage readily with feedback and iteration Strong writers and communicators who take visible pride in the quality of their work and the accuracy of their details Self-directed people who are comfortable creating structure where none exists, figuring things out independently, and taking ownership of their own career Resourceful relationship builders who proactively reach out, build trust across teams, and adapt their style to different personalities and Consultant preferences People who are comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and the pace of client service Team-oriented colleagues with a “no task too small” mindset who contribute beyond their immediate responsibilities People with poise, maturity, and professional presence IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU? We would rather you have a clear picture now than discover it after you join. The role consistently requires the following. If these conditions do not match what you are looking for, this may not be the right fit: Earned scope rather than immediate ownership . Client relationship ownership and independent assessment leadership expand as demonstrated quality and trust are established, not from day one. Working without a defined process . Engagements vary by Solution, client, and Consultant. The role requires building your own structure, workflows, and standards in the absence of fixed procedures. Extensive writing and multiple revision cycles . Writing is an essential function. Deliverables routinely undergo several rounds of substantive feedback and rework before reaching the client. Owning your own project management . The role carries end-to-end accountability for timelines, coordination, and follow-up. Dedicated project management support is not provided. Building internal relationships that influence staffing . Engagement assignments are shaped in part by internal trust and reputation, which the role requires you to actively develop. Capability-based advancement . Progression to Consultant is assessed against a published framework and takes time; it is not tenure-driven or accelerated on request. Limited early opportunity to independently lead assessments . Because our work sits at the C-suite and board level, independent assessment leadership comes later than at firms working deeper in the organization. Influence through partnership rather than sole authority . Decisions are reached collaboratively with Consultants and engagement teams. A distinct business from Executive Search . LAS has different client work, methodologies, and career paths. CRITICAL CAPABILITIES FOR SUCCESS These capabilities form the basis of the LAS Associate Development Framework and of the assessment of performance and promotion readiness. We share them openly so you know what you are signing up for and how you will be evaluated. Project management Manages overall projects and oversees the team's collective efforts to drive the cadence and flow of client outcomes. Owns the project workplan across multiple workstreams; organizes and facilitates team touchpoints and keeps the team accountable Takes ownership of whole projects and serves as a day-to-day point of contact with the client Manages multiple engagements with competing deadlines; sets expectations, clarifies roles, and avoids duplication of effort Anticipates challenges, adjusts priorities, and pushes back internally as appropriate Remains calm under pressure and delivers on commitments, or raises slippage early with a proposed solution Uses technology and AI-enabled tools to improve project efficiency, with appropriate validation Client insights Gathers nuanced insight from sophisticated data collection and delivers it in a way that is relevant for clients and resonates with participants. Establishes productive relationships with clients, participants, and colleagues across the Firm, and builds a personal brand defined by reliability and collaboration Adapts style to the audience, coaching with participants, business-insight-driven with clients, and remains composed under pressure Contributes meaningfully in debriefs, assessments, workshops, and client conversations without being prompted Coordinates team efforts on complex projects; unblocks obstacles and helps create consensus Places team goals ahead of individual goals; volunteers to share workload and shares information generously while being rigorous about confidentiality Business and market knowledge Obtains and incorporates knowledge across one or more of our Solutions to enhance client work in a meaningful way. Builds deep knowledge of the concepts and principles underlying our assessment, culture, team, development, succession, and performance acceleration frameworks, and can teach others Develops foundational business acumen, financial statements, executive role responsibilities, organizational structures, and operating models, and applies them to the client context Shows curiosity about the bigger picture surrounding an assignment, taking a systems view that considers company and industry context Understands how Search and LAS work together, and navigates internal resources, materials, and experts to bring the best of the Firm to client work Stays current on business, economic, and leadership advisory news, and brings relevant insight to teams and clients Developing self and others Seeks and provides feedback; coaches and mentors to improve team performance; modifies own performance based on input. Proactively seeks feedback from every project team and demonstrates progress against development areas over time Takes personal responsibility for career development, engaging mentors and sponsors, and articulating aspirations clearly Provides balanced, behavioral feedback to junior colleagues and creates opportunities for their development Serves as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor and supports the integration of new colleagues Firm values Champions the Firm's values, culture, and Code of Conduct; engages, participates, and collaborates with others. Demonstrates alignment to Firm values in everyday behavior; is professional, cordial, and engaging in all settings Brings cultural awareness and sensitivity to every interaction with colleagues and clients Participates actively in office, practice, and Firm-wide activities, and builds a network beyond LAS Leverages AI responsibly, maintaining human accountability for client data, confidential information, and intellectual property Represents Spencer Stuart well and lives by the Code of Conduct Career path and progression Level: Associate What changes: Own workstreams end-to-end; manage substantial project components with increasing autonomy; build trusted client relationships; synthesize data into clear, client-relevant insight; create structure from ambiguity; begin developing others intentionally. The base compensation range for this position is $100,000 –150,000 per year.
